docs.title: About
docs.text:
I am Prakash Kumar, a technical writer focused on making complex software easier to understand, adopt, and support. My work spans AI documentation, cloud documentation, API documentation, product documentation, knowledge bases, SOPs, release notes, and docs-as-code workflows.

I write for the people who depend on documentation to make decisions and complete work: developers, administrators, support teams, implementation teams, product managers, engineering teams, and business users. My goal is simple: reduce confusion, improve self-service, and make documentation feel like part of the product experience.

docs.title: Documentation Philosophy
docs.text:
Good documentation should be accurate, findable, maintainable, and respectful of the reader's time. I do not see documentation as a final delivery artifact that appears after the product is done. I see it as a product surface that helps users understand what exists, what matters, what to do next, and how to recover when something goes wrong.

My documentation philosophy is built around four principles:

  • Start with the audience

    Documentation should match the reader's role, context, vocabulary, and technical depth.

  • Design the information architecture

    Strong navigation, consistent labels, and useful categories make content easier to scan and maintain.

  • Write for action

    Procedures, examples, prerequisites, expected results, and troubleshooting paths help readers finish real tasks.

  • Keep content maintainable

    Markdown, Git, MkDocs, Sphinx, reusable patterns, and review workflows help documentation stay current.

docs.title: Writing Process
docs.text:
My writing process balances product understanding, technical validation, and reader experience.

  1. Understand the audience and goal Identify who the content is for, what they need to accomplish, and what level of detail they expect.

  2. Collect source information Review product behavior, SME inputs, API details, UI flows, release notes, tickets, and available engineering references.

  3. Design the content structure Define the page type, heading structure, information flow, navigation placement, and related content paths.

  4. Write and test the draft Create clear Markdown content with prerequisites, steps, examples, notes, warnings, and validation points.

  5. Review and refine Incorporate SME feedback, check terminology, remove ambiguity, improve scanability, and prepare the content for publication.

  6. Maintain and improve Update content through product changes, support insights, search behavior, release cycles, and documentation audits.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.text:
Overview: API reference and developer-facing documentation for REST API usage, authentication, request and response formats, and error handling.

Objective: Help developers understand how to authenticate, call endpoints, interpret responses, troubleshoot errors, and integrate APIs into their workflows.

Audience: Developers, solution architects, technical leads, implementation teams.

Tools Used: Markdown, OpenAPI, Swagger, Postman, Git, GitHub, Confluence.

Technologies: REST API, JSON, XML, authentication, HTTP methods, status codes.

Writing Process: Reviewed API behavior and source inputs, structured endpoint documentation, defined prerequisites, documented examples, added error guidance, and prepared content for technical review.

Deliverables: API references, authentication guides, error code documentation, integration notes, Postman-oriented usage guidance.

Screenshots: Add endpoint reference screenshots after sample content is approved.

Downloads: Add sanitized API sample PDFs or Markdown exports when available.

Lessons Learned: API documentation works best when reference details, conceptual context, and troubleshooting guidance are connected instead of separated into isolated pages.

Tools Used: Markdown, MkDocs, Jira, Confluence, GitHub.

Deliverables: Release notes, change summaries, feature descriptions, upgrade notes, known issue content.

Lessons Learned: Release notes are most useful when they explain user impact, not just implementation details.

Context: Provide source information and constraints.

Review: Check accuracy, completeness, and suitability.

docs.title: Developer Guides
docs.text: Developer documentation helps technical readers move from concept to implementation. I write developer guides that define prerequisites, explain architecture context, show task flows, and connect API details with practical usage.

docs.title: Developer Documentation Types
docs.text:
• Integration guides Step-by-step flows for connecting systems, services, APIs, or product features.

  • Developer onboarding Setup instructions, local environment guidance, tools, and first successful workflow.

docs.title: Writing Pattern
docs.text:
1. Define the developer goal.
  2. List prerequisites and assumptions.
  3. Explain the system or feature context.
  4. Provide implementation steps.
  5. Add examples, expected results, and validation checks.
  6. Link to API reference, configuration, and troubleshooting pages.

docs.text: Installation documentation helps users set up a product or system correctly the first time. I write installation guides that are sequenced, testable, and easy to follow under real implementation conditions.

docs.title: Installation Guide Components
docs.text:

  • Validation Checks that confirm the installation completed successfully.

  • Recovery guidance Common installation issues, causes, and resolution paths.

docs.title: Installation Checklist
docs.text:
• Define supported environments.
  • Confirm required permissions.
  • Document files, packages, or dependencies.
  • Sequence setup steps in the order users perform them.
  • Add expected results after major steps.
  • Include troubleshooting and rollback notes where applicable.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Structure
docs.text:
• Symptoms What the user sees, including messages, failed states, or unexpected behavior.

  • Causes Likely reasons the issue occurs, written in plain technical language.

  • Resolution Ordered steps that help the user recover or narrow the issue.

  • Validation How to confirm the issue is resolved.

docs.title: Article Pattern
